title: The Energy Problem

beats.narrativeText: Power shortages continue affecting the outpost.
Restoring power isn't as simple as turning everything on at once.
The learner analyses how electricity is distributed through the station and what each system requires.
Solving a series of circuit challenges reveals how the station's power network is connected.
The learner must prioritise essential systems and balance them against the energy actually available.
The learner works out the correct sequence to safely restore power.
The learner records their reasoning for why each system was prioritised in that order.
Major systems return online, and evidence suggests the expedition deliberately conserved power for a reason not yet understood.

activities.title: Analyse Energy Requirements
activities.storyContext: Power shortages continue affecting the outpost, and every system has different energy needs.
activities.instructions: Work out how much energy each station system requires to operate.
activities.output: A list of energy requirements for each system.

activities.title: Solve Circuit Challenges
activities.storyContext: The station's power network connects every system together.
activities.instructions: Solve a series of circuit challenges to understand how the power network is connected.
activities.output: Solved circuit challenges showing the power network layout.

activities.title: Prioritise Essential Systems
activities.storyContext: Rather than simply turning everything on, the learner must balance available energy against operational priorities.
activities.instructions: Decide which systems should be restored first, given the limited energy available.
activities.output: A prioritised list of systems to restore.

activities.title: Record Reasoning
activities.storyContext: A good plan can always be explained.
activities.instructions: Write down the reasoning behind your restoration sequence.
activities.output: A written explanation of the restoration sequence.

activities.title: Design an Emergency Power Plan
activities.storyContext: A good Explorer plans ahead for the next emergency, not just the current one.
activities.instructions: Design an emergency power plan for the station in case of a future shortage.

activities.title: Electricity in Extreme Environments
activities.storyContext: Outpost Echo isn't the only remote station that has to solve power problems.
activities.instructions: Find out how remote research stations generate electricity in extreme environments.
activities.output: None required — this is an open investigation.

prompts: How did you decide which systems to restore first, and why?

discussionPoints: Why is it important to prioritise which systems to restore first?
What would happen if every system was restored at once?
parentGuide.assessment: Look for a restoration sequence that is justified by reasoning about priorities, not a random order.

completionCriteria: Energy requirements analysed, circuit challenges solved, and essential systems prioritised with recorded reasoning.
